title: Passion Integration in Your Awareness Journal
opening: Keep a useful observation for the next time a pursuit’s value and difficulty change. You do not need to record every moment.

labels.example: Compare the context, not just the slogan
labels.figure: Comparison of learner-question preparation and schedule-only preparation; the possible value relationship remains uncertain.
labels.comparisonPrompt: Edit the two notes if a clearer separation would help. The example is illustrative, not your experience.
labels.broadLabel: Too general to guide the next choice
labels.practicePrompt: Choose one situation where the value–difficulty relationship changed. Keep what happened separate from what you think it meant. Include only details you may want to find later; dates and people are optional.
labels.event: What happened? Record observed details and relevant conditions
labels.value: What value do you think appeared here? This is your interpretation; leave it uncertain if you do not know
labels.difficulty: Which particular difficulty did you accept for that value?
labels.change: What changed in the relationship between value and difficulty? What else may explain it?
labels.next: What will you notice next time?
labels.patterns: If this recurs, which earlier entries might you compare? Leave blank if this is a first entry
labels.private: This note is private to you. Save a partial draft or leave optional details blank; a journal is not a report of every moment.
labels.sourceHint: Supplied recovered manuscript, p. 43 (82-page source edition).

source.quote: Passion Integration in Your Awareness Journal retains the learning: where value appeared, which difficulty you accepted for it, where the relationship changed and what to notice next. Review recurring patterns across entries.
source.attribution: Supplied recovered manuscript; authorship/adoption of every wording is not independently established.
source.boundary: Keep the situation with the conclusion. What counts as value is your interpretation; label it as such. If later conditions differ, update the entry instead of reapplying it as a rule. Do not turn the journal into a required log of every moment or treat an abandoned pursuit as a personal failure.

example.facts: Preparation answered a real learner question. In another case, the work was only to maintain a posting schedule; the teacher felt drained.
example.meaning: The first preparation may have served the value of helping a learner understand. The schedule-only task may not have served that value in the same way.
example.reading: The short slogan loses the conditions. The two editable notes retain an event account and a separate interpretation, so the teacher can find the relevant distinction when choosing the next task.

connections: Related practices: Self-Discovery Cycle (M157) captures, reflects, and integrates; Keep the pursuit viable (M160) tracks internal willingness to continue.
